Changes to bin collections

From 1 April, general waste will be collected every two weeks instead of every week, and your collection day may change. Recycling and food waste collections stay the same. This page explains what changes, how to find your new day, and how to ask for a larger bin.

What will change

General waste will be collected every two weeks. Recycling will still be collected every two weeks, on the week the general waste is not. Food waste will still be collected every week, on the same day as now.

The contract with the company that empties the bins ends in March. The council asked residents what they wanted from the next contract, and more than six thousand people answered the survey or came to one of the meetings held in libraries across the district.

Find your new collection day

The council will send every household a letter with a new calendar in March. You can also look up your day on the council website by entering your postcode, or ask at any library. The calendar shows the colour of the bin to put out each week, and the dates of the extra collections after the holidays.

If you do not get a letter by the end of March, or the calendar shows the wrong address, call the council on the number at the bottom of this page. Lines are open from 9am to 5pm, Monday to Friday.

Ask for a larger bin

Households with six or more people, or with someone who uses nappies or medical waste, can ask for a larger bin. The form to ask for one will open in February, and the council will deliver the bins before the new collections start. You do not need to pay for a larger bin.

Why the council made this choice

Collecting general waste every two weeks costs less and encourages people to recycle more. Councils that made the same change found that the amount of waste sent to landfill fell by about a fifth in the first year. The money saved will be used to keep the recycling centres open on Sundays.
